property_summary: Only the owner can successfully call withdrawAll; calls by non-owners revert.
Only the owner address can successfully call withdrawAll, so calls from non-owner addresses revert.
After owner calls withdrawAll(recipient), the contract's entire balance is transferred to the provided recipient (not left with or sent to the caller).
When withdrawAll is invoked by the owner it should not revert (i.e., complete) for any recipient address.

If anyone other than owner calls withdrawAll it reverts, and if the owner calls withdrawAll then the contract's balance is transferred out of the contract (so address(c).balance becomes zero) and call does not revert.
If the owner calls withdrawAll, the call must succeed (not revert).
When the owner calls withdrawAll, the call completes (does not revert) and the contract's balance becomes zero afterward.

For any caller who is the owner and any recipient address, calling withdrawAll(recipient) transfers the contract's balance to the provided recipient (so address(c).balance == 0 afterwards); the mutant that sends funds to msg.sender instead breaks this: for some recipient inputs the contract's balance may still be 0 but the recipient doesn't receive funds (and the owner does), observable via recipient's balance change — we assert that after withdrawAll(recipient) the contract's balance is zero and the recipient's balance increased by the contract balance (this holds for reference but is violated by the mutant for some inputs).

For any caller who is the owner and any recipient address, calling withdrawAll(recipient) transfers the contract's entire balance to the provided recipient (so after the call address(c).balance == 0 and the recipient's balance increased by the pre-call contract balance); the mutant that sends to msg.sender breaks this because the owner — not the provided recipient — receives the funds for some inputs.

For any owner caller and any recipient address that is a contract able to receive Ether, calling withdrawAll(recipient) causes the recipient contract's balance to increase by the contract's pre-call balance (and c's balance to become zero) — the mutant that pays msg.sender instead will not increase the recipient contract's balance when the recipient != owner, so this property is violated for some inputs.

For every owner-invoked withdrawAll(recipient) call, the reference contract sends its entire balance to the supplied recipient (so recipient balance increases by pre-call contract balance and address(c).balance becomes 0); the mutant instead sends to msg.sender (owner), violating this for some recipient addresses when recipient != owner.

For any owner caller and any recipient address, withdrawAll(recipient) always results in the contract's balance becoming zero and the specified recipient receiving the entire pre-call contract balance; the mutant that pays msg.sender instead will (for some recipient != owner) leave the recipient's balance unchanged while the owner gains the funds, violating this rule.
After a successful withdrawAll call by the owner, the balance of contract C becomes zero.
withdrawAll never reverts when called by the contract owner
If caller equals the stored owner of c, then calling c.withdrawAll(caller) should not revert (i.e., reverted == (caller != c.owner())).
If reverted is true then caller is not the stored owner of c, and if caller equals the stored owner then the call does not revert (i.e., reverted == (caller != c.owner())).
The call reverts exactly when the caller is not the stored owner: reverted == (caller != c.owner()).

For any caller that is the owner and any initial contract balance, calling withdrawAll transfers the entire contract balance out so address(c).balance becomes zero; the mutant that comments out the transfer can leave a non-zero balance for some inputs (owner calls with positive balance).
After owner calls withdrawAll, the recipient receives the entire contract balance (so contract balance becomes zero).
If the caller is the contract owner, withdrawAll must revert (i.e., only non-owner calls can succeed).
If this test contract is the owner of c, then invoking c.withdrawAll(recipient) must revert (i.e., isCallerOwner == reverted).
If this test contract is the observed owner of c, then calling c.withdrawAll(recipient) should revert (isCallerOwner == reverted).
If this test contract is the observed owner of c (c.owner() == address(this)), then calling c.withdrawAll(recipient) reverts (isCallerOwner == reverted).

For any caller who is the owner and any deposited balance, calling withdrawAll(recipient) transfers the entire contract balance to recipient (leaving c.balance == 0); the mutant that only transfers half breaks this by leaving a nonzero contract balance for some inputs.

For any caller equal to owner and any initial contract balance funded by some sender, after calling withdrawAll(recipient) the reference C always leaves address(c).balance == 0 (transfers entire balance), whereas the mutant that sends only half will leave a nonzero contract balance for some inputs.
After a successful withdrawAll by owner, contract balance becomes zero (all funds transferred out).
If withdrawAll is called by a non-owner it must revert (reverted == true); only an owner call may succeed.

withdrawAll called by any address always reverts (i.e., non-success) when the contract's owner is not this caller and the contract has nonzero balance — original reverts for non-owner, mutant may not.
If caller is not the owner, withdrawAll must revert (i.e., only the owner can successfully call withdrawAll).
When the provided caller is not the owner, withdrawAll must revert.

For any recipient and any contract balance sent in the withdrawAll call, the reference contract transfers the entire contract balance to the specified recipient so that address(c).balance == 0 afterwards; the mutant may perform an extra transfer to owner (even of zero value but changing observed behavior in some cases) which can make the final contract balance differ from zero for some inputs.

For any caller and any recipient, after withdrawAll(...) completes the reference contract C always has zero balance (address(c).balance == 0); the mutant can cause a nonzero final contract balance for some inputs when the recipient is a contract whose fallback/receive reverts or forwards gas in a way that changes observable transfers, so the invariant can be violated.

For any caller and any recipient, when the owner calls withdrawAll the reference contract always ends with zero balance (address(c).balance == 0) after forwarding the entire balance to the recipient; the mutant that adds an extra transfer to owner can cause the final contract balance to be non-zero for some recipient behaviors (specifically a recipient contract that reverts on transfer), breaking this invariant.

For any recipient and any initial contract balance funded by the owner call, calling withdrawAll(recipient) as owner always results in the contract's balance being zero (reference); the mutant that adds an extra transfer to owner can cause the final contract balance to be nonzero for some recipient behaviors, so checking address(c).balance == 0 distinguishes them.

For every recipient address and any contract balance funded to C, when the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the reference contract always leaves C with zero balance (it forwards the entire balance to the recipient); the mutant that inserts an extra transfer statement can change observable behavior when the recipient reverts on receiving funds, causing the final address(c).balance to be non-zero for some inputs.
After a successful withdrawAll call initiated by the owner, the contract's balance must be zero (i.e., all funds are forwarded or the call reverts).
If withdrawAll is called by the owner, the call must not revert (i.e., owner-initiated withdrawAll always completes).

If withdrawAll is called by the owner when the contract has a positive balance, the call must complete (not revert) and the caller's address must not receive any Ether from the contract (i.e., this test's balance does not increase).
